venues.name: Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc
venues.note: The legend of the Riviera since 1870, a white palace on its own cape, with the sea-cut Eden-Roc pool the coast's most famous set piece.

venues.name: Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat, A Four Seasons Hotel
venues.note: A Belle Époque palace on seven hectares at the tip of the coast's most exclusive cape, private, forested and utterly serene.

venues.name: Château de la Chèvre d'Or
venues.note: A medieval eyrie clinging to the cliff of Èze village, 400m above the sea, the Riviera's most romantic address, with two-starred dining in-house.

venues.name: La Réserve de Beaulieu & Spa
venues.note: A rose-pink Italianate villa on its own harbour since 1880, a hushed, aristocratic grande dame between Nice and Monaco.

venues.name: Le Negresco
venues.note: Nice's own pink-domed palace on the Promenade des Anglais, a private, family-owned house of art and theatre, a national monument since 1974.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Anantara Plaza Nice Hotel
venues.note: An 1848 Belle Époque landmark off the Promenade, reborn by Anantara, Nice's most polished contemporary luxury, with a rooftop over the old town.

venues.name: Hôtel Martinez, Cannes (Hyatt Unbound Collection)
venues.note: The Art Deco grande dame of the Croisette, the address of the Film Festival, with the largest private beach in Cannes and a starred kitchen.

venues.name: Cap Estel
venues.note: A private peninsula of five acres between Nice and Monaco, a villa hotel wrapped by the sea on three sides, screened from the world.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Hôtel Barrière Le Majestic Cannes
venues.note: A white 1926 palace at the head of the Croisette, grand, gracious and at the very centre of Cannes' glamour.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Mirazur
venues.note: Mauro Colagreco's cliff-garden temple above the Italian border, seed-to-plate cooking from twelve acres of biodynamic terraces, once the best restaurant on earth.

venues.name: La Chèvre d'Or
venues.note: Two-starred cooking suspended on the cliff of Èze village, the whole coast falling away below, chef Tom Meyer, Meilleur Ouvrier de France.

venues.name: Flaveur
venues.note: The Tourteaux brothers' two-star in central Nice, bold, spice-laced Mediterranean cooking, with Indian notes woven through local seafood.

venues.name: La Palme d'Or
venues.note: The Art Deco fine-dining room of the Hôtel Martinez, relaunched under Jean Imbert, the star table of the Croisette.

venues.name: Le Restaurant des Rois
venues.note: Julien Roucheteau's gastronomic room at La Réserve de Beaulieu, haute cuisine in a sumptuous seafront salon.

venues.name: Le Chantecler
venues.note: The starred dining room of Le Negresco, Virginie Basselot, Meilleur Ouvrier de France, cooking Mediterranean haute gastronomie in a wood-panelled salon.

venues.name: Louroc
venues.note: The starred restaurant of Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc, sea-facing Mediterranean cooking at the Riviera's most legendary address.

venues.name: JAN
venues.note: Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen's intimate 20-seater near the port, French technique threaded with a South African soul.

venues.name: Pure & V
venues.note: Chef Pinja Paakkonen's Nordic-inflected kitchen in central Nice, with one of the coast's most characterful natural-wine lists.

venues.name: Racines - Bruno Cirino
venues.note: Bruno Cirino's 'kitchen-garden cuisine', a single set menu of perfectly-ripe Mediterranean produce, largely vegetarian and farm-driven.

venues.name: L'Aromate
venues.note: Mickaël Gracieux's refined, produce-driven cooking in the heart of Nice, a quietly serious one-star.

venues.name: Peixes
venues.note: Fish and seafood served tapas-style in a blue-and-white tiled bistro near the opera, vibrant, Mediterranean-meets-South-American, and much loved.

venues.name: Le Bistrot de Jan
venues.note: The relaxed sibling of starred JAN, the same South African-French spirit at an easier, everyday pitch.

venues.name: Maison Barale
venues.note: A century-old Niçois family kitchen in Vieux Nice, the real ravioli, daube and socca of the old town.

venues.name: La Merenda
venues.note: Dominique Le Stanc's tiny, cash-only Niçoise counter, a former two-star chef cooking the humble classics of Nice by hand.
credentials: A celebrated Niçois institution, chef Dominique Le Stanc (ex-Le Chantecler ★★)

venues.name: Promenade des Anglais
venues.note: The seven-kilometre Belle Époque seafront curving along the Baie des Anges, its blue chairs facing the water and the ochre Négresco dome behind. An unhurried morning stroll here, ice-cream in hand, is the Riviera at its most effortless, perfect for three generations moving at their own pace.
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera

venues.name: Vieux Nice (Old Town)
venues.note: A warren of ochre-and-terracotta lanes, baroque churches and shaded piazzas where laundry strings hang above artisan gelato shops. This is the emotional heart of Nice, small enough to wander with children, layered enough to reward a return each evening for aperitivo.
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera

venues.name: Cours Saleya Market
venues.note: The famous flower-and-produce market, cut peonies, Menton lemons, tapenade, socca fresh off the copper pan, with a Monday antiques market in place of flowers. A vivid morning for the family, and a generous window into Niçoise produce for veg-leaning palates.

venues.name: Colline du Château (Castle Hill)
venues.note: The green headland between the old town and the port, crowned by a man-made waterfall and the definitive view down over the terracotta rooftops and the sweep of the Baie des Anges. Reachable by a discreet free lift for those who prefer not to climb.
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera

venues.name: Musée Matisse
venues.note: A red-ochre Genoese villa set in an olive grove, holding one of the world's most complete Matisse collections, the artist lived and died in Nice and is buried nearby. Intimate, sunlit and rarely crowded, it pairs naturally with a picnic under the Cimiez olive trees.

venues.name: Musée National Marc Chagall
venues.note: Purpose-built to hold Chagall's luminous Biblical Message cycle, seventeen large canvases glowing in a calm, light-filled space he helped design. A short, deeply moving visit that lands equally with art lovers and first-timers.

venues.name: MAMAC, Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
venues.note: A striking marble-clad building holding Nice's own School (Yves Klein, Arman, the Nouveaux Réalistes) plus Warhol and Lichtenstein, with a rooftop terrace looking over the city. The contemporary counterweight to the city's Belle Époque grandeur.

venues.name: Cimiez Quarter & Roman Ruins
venues.note: The genteel hill district of grand winter-palace hotels turned apartments, with Roman baths, an amphitheatre and a Franciscan monastery garden overlooking the coast. The refined, residential Nice the aristocracy chose, best explored slowly.
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera

venues.name: Port Lympia (Old Port)
venues.note: The photogenic old harbour framed by tall Italianate façades, where fishing boats sit beside superyachts and the seafood restaurants of the quai spill onto the water. The natural place to board a private charter or dine facing the masts at dusk.
credentials: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera

venues.name: Place Masséna & Promenade du Paillon
venues.note: The grand red-arcaded square with its checkerboard paving and mirror-fountain, opening onto a long green park of water jets and lawns that runs to the sea. A cooling, kid-friendly spine through the city on hot afternoons.

venues.name: Monaco & Monte-Carlo
venues.note: The gilded sovereign city-state fifteen minutes along the coast, palace, harbour of superyachts, Belle Époque casino and grand hotels stacked on a rock over the sea. The Riviera's concentrated shot of glamour, best done by private driver for a day.

venues.name: Casino de Monte-Carlo
venues.note: Charles Garnier's Belle Époque temple of gaming, all gilt, marble and painted ceilings, facing the manicured casino gardens. Even without a chip on the table, the salons and the Café de Paris terrace opposite are pure theatre, jacket and passport advised.

venues.name: Prince's Palace of Monaco
venues.note: The Grimaldi family's residence high on the Rock, with lavish State Apartments open in season and the daily changing of the guard at 11:55 in the square outside. History and pageantry with one of the best harbour views in the principality.

venues.name: Oceanographic Museum of Monaco
venues.note: A monumental institution founded by Prince Albert I, clinging to the cliff eighty-five metres above the sea, with grand aquaria, a shark lagoon and a rooftop terrace. Genuinely spellbinding for children and a serene stop for adults.

venues.name: The Monaco Grand Prix Circuit
venues.note: The legendary street circuit runs through the everyday town, the Casino square, the Fairmont hairpin, the tunnel, the harbour chicane. Trace it on foot any day of the year, or watch it come alive over the late-May race weekend from a harbourside berth.

venues.name: Jardin Exotique d'Èze
venues.note: A cascade of cacti and succulents crowning the ruined castle at the very top of Èze, opening onto a dizzying panorama that on clear days reaches to Corsica. Small, sculptural and quietly the finest view in the village.

venues.name: Villefranche-sur-Mer
venues.note: A jewel-box fishing port on one of the Mediterranean's deepest natural harbours, with a rose-and-ochre old town, a Cocteau-painted chapel and a sheltered beach. Ten minutes from Nice yet a world softer, a favourite anchorage for private yachts.

venues.name: Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat
venues.note: The discreet green peninsula of billionaires' villas and pine-shaded coastal paths, with a low-key port and some of the most exclusive addresses on the coast. Precisely the kind of quiet, moneyed seclusion the Riviera's oldest fortunes prize.

venues.name: Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild
venues.note: Baroness Béatrice de Rothschild's rose-pink palace on the crest of Cap Ferrat, ringed by nine themed gardens, French, Spanish, Florentine, Japanese, around a musical fountain. The Riviera's most exquisite house-and-garden day, and candlelit on summer evenings.

venues.name: Villa Kérylos
venues.note: A faithful recreation of an ancient Greek villa built on a rocky point over the sea by archaeologist Théodore Reinach, complete with mosaics, frescoes and Antiquity-inspired furniture. A serene, scholarly counterpoint to the coast's Belle Époque excess.

venues.name: Antibes Old Town & Marché Provençal
venues.note: Ramparts against the sea, cobbled lanes and a superb covered Provençal market of cheeses, olives, flowers and produce. Antibes wears its history lightly and dines beautifully, an easy, atmospheric half-day with the family.

venues.name: Musée Picasso, Antibes
venues.note: Set in the seafront Château Grimaldi where Picasso worked for a joyous few months in 1946, holding the paintings and ceramics he left behind. Compact, sunlit and looking straight onto the Mediterranean that fills the canvases.

venues.name: Cap d'Antibes & Sentier du Littoral
venues.note: The legendary green cape of grand villas and the fabled Eden-Roc, ringed by a coastal footpath past secret coves and the so-called Billionaires' Bay. Old-money glamour at its most photographed, walk the path, then a private lunch behind the pines.

venues.name: Port Vauban & the Superyacht Quay
venues.note: One of the Mediterranean's largest marinas, its 'Quai des Milliardaires' berthing the world's most extraordinary superyachts beneath the old fort. A striking evening walk, and the practical launch point for a day at sea.

venues.name: Cannes, La Croisette
venues.note: The palm-lined boulevard of palace hotels, designer flagships and private beach clubs where the film festival unfurls its red carpet each May. Glamour worn openly, dress the part and take an evening promenade past the Carlton and Martinez.

venues.name: Le Suquet, Old Cannes
venues.note: The steep original village above the port, its stepped lanes climbing to a watchtower and a panorama over the bay. A far quieter, more soulful Cannes than the Croisette, best at golden hour before dinner on the Rue Saint-Antoine.

venues.name: Saint-Paul-de-Vence
venues.note: A ravishing fortified hill village of galleries and stone ramparts that drew Chagall, Signac and half of mid-century Paris; Chagall is buried in its cemetery. Wander the lanes, then lunch at the storied La Colombe d'Or among its Picassos and Mirós.

venues.name: Fondation Maeght
venues.note: One of Europe's great private art foundations, a modernist building set in pine woods with a Giacometti courtyard, a Miró labyrinth and Braque pools, freshly expanded for its 60th anniversary. A pilgrimage for anyone serious about 20th-century art.

venues.name: Grasse, Perfume Capital
venues.note: The inland town that has scented the world for centuries, where the historic houses of Fragonard, Galimard and Molinard open their workshops. Compose your own bespoke fragrance in a private atelier, an intimate, memorable family afternoon.

venues.name: Menton
venues.note: The last town before Italy, a pastel amphitheatre of lemon groves and gardens basking in the Riviera's mildest microclimate, host to the famous February Lemon Festival. Softly Italianate and blissfully unhurried, a gentle day for all generations.

venues.name: Jardin Serre de la Madone & Menton's Gardens
venues.note: Menton's exceptional climate nurtures a constellation of botanical gardens, the terraced Serre de la Madone, the exotic Val Rahmeh, the Fontana Rosa. A tranquil, fragrant counterpoint for garden lovers away from the beach crowds.

venues.name: Gorges du Verdon
venues.note: Europe's grandest canyon, where turquoise water winds between limestone walls hundreds of metres deep, opening onto the emerald Lac de Sainte-Croix. A dramatic full-day inland expedition of clifftop drives, kayaking and the lavender plateaux beyond.

venues.name: Roquebrune-Cap-Martin
venues.note: A medieval hill village crowned by one of France's oldest castle keeps, with a coastal cape below of villas, pines and Le Corbusier's tiny Cabanon. Quiet, storied and perched between Monaco and Menton, a graceful hour or two off the main track.

venues.name: Beaches & Private Beach Clubs of Nice
venues.note: Along the Baie des Anges, a run of managed beach clubs offer loungers, umbrellas and service on the famous pebble shore, from Blue Beach to the hotel-run establishments. Reserve a front-row set, the discreet way to enjoy the sea in comfort.

venues.name: Plage de Paloma & Cap Ferrat Coves
venues.note: The elegant crescent of Paloma Beach on the tip of Cap Ferrat, with its long-loved beach restaurant and clear, sheltered water. The insiders' choice for a refined, uncrowded swim reached by coastal path or private tender.

venues.name: Pampelonne-style Days at Juan-les-Pins
venues.note: The lively pine-fringed bay next to Cap d'Antibes, birthplace of Riviera beach glamour in the Jazz Age and still lined with sandy beach clubs and evening bars. A more animated, youthful counterpoint for the family's beach day.

venues.name: Private Yacht Charter along the Coast
venues.note: The truest way to experience the Côte d'Azur, cast off from Nice, Antibes or Cannes to anchor off Cap Ferrat, the Lérins islands and the coves of Cap d'Antibes for a swim and lunch aboard. Privacy, freedom and the coast seen from its best angle.

venues.name: Socca & Niçoise Table
venues.note: Nice has its own cuisine, chickpea socca hot off the griddle, pan bagnat, ratatouille, tender-veg tians and pissaladière, much of it naturally vegetable-led. Graze the old town's institutions, or arrange a private Niçoise tasting for the family.

venues.name: Vence & the Chapelle du Rosaire (Matisse Chapel)
venues.note: A walled town near Saint-Paul whose true treasure is the little Rosary Chapel that Matisse designed and considered his masterpiece, pure white walls lit by cobalt-and-gold glass. A quiet, luminous stop for those who love him.

venues.name: Mougins, Hilltop Village of Gastronomy
venues.note: A pristine spiral village above Cannes where Picasso spent his last years, now a haven of galleries and celebrated tables. A polished, art-and-food afternoon away from the coast, easily paired with Grasse.

venues.name: Musée Jean Cocteau, Menton
venues.note: Menton's tribute to the poet-artist Jean Cocteau, spanning the little seafront Bastion he decorated himself and the collection he left the town. A charming, human-scaled museum to close a slow day near the Italian border.

venues.name: Le Relais
venues.note: Le Negresco's walnut-panelled bar since 1913, a century of Riviera legend from Delon to the Beatles, hushed by day, jazz-lit by night.
credentials: Within Le Negresco, Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Le Bar du Ciel, Anantara Plaza Nice
venues.note: A rooftop bar over the old town and the sea, cocktails at golden hour above the centre of Nice.
credentials: Within Anantara Plaza Nice, MICHELIN Guide Hotel (Selected)

venues.name: Le Bar Churchill, Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc
venues.note: The clubby bar of the Riviera's most legendary hotel, a Negroni among the pines, where the coast's glamour has gathered for a century.
credentials: Within Hôtel du Cap-Eden-Roc, MICHELIN Key (2025), Oetker Collection

venues.name: Bar du Cap, Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat
venues.note: An elegant, low-lit bar in a Four Seasons palace on the cape, quiet, grown-up and framed by seven hectares of garden.
credentials: Within Grand-Hôtel du Cap-Ferrat, A Four Seasons Hotel, MICHELIN Key (2025)

venues.name: Movida / Vieux Nice bar quarter
venues.note: The lanes around the Cours Saleya and Rue de la Préfecture, where Nice's own late night gathers, spilling from bar to bar.
